Oh, Mac stuff. Out of my element there, sorry.

Ask the band how they recorded their guitar tracks. From what you're saying it sounds like they had a bad contact if they were using DIs , or it could be fuzzy amp sounds. The best way to deal with that is to get them to record it right.

You could also use a decrackling/denoising software. Look up Izotope RX, its one of my favorite editing tools.

If you have been given them to mix, there may be a discrepancy between the kHz's. The crackling you described sounds like the guitars were recorded at 44.1kHz and you are mixing at 48kHz or reverse. But it might be that your setup is allright and they recorded it badly.

  • if the crackling is exactly the same everytime you play the isolated track, and you are able to see the pops in the wav file, it's in the recording and you're in for a lot of work

  • if the crackling is different every time you play the isolated track, there is an error in your setup, and I would start with examining the kHz's.
